## Learning outcome

Distinguish causal order from wall-clock timestamp order.

::: {.notes}
Prerequisites: Lectures 01 and 03. This is a sample deck for the proposed syllabus, not a full lecture.
:::

## Worked scenario

The registration service sends a confirmation event. A notification worker receives it and sends an email. The worker clock happens to be behind the service clock.

::: {.notes}
Different machines can report different wall-clock times for related events. Message exchange gives another ordering rule: a message must be sent before that same message is received. This helps reason about causality without assuming perfectly synchronized clocks.
:::

## Discussion and recap

Can the email have an earlier timestamp without having caused the registration?

**Takeaway:** Reason about causal dependencies before interpreting timestamps.

::: {.notes}
Ask students to name assumptions before proposing a solution. The complete planned scope is recorded in the lecture brief.
:::
